accident_report:
Vehicle Initialization
On a straight, uphill, single-direction roadway with three lanes (lane 1 on the far right to lane 3 on the left), bordered on the left by a continuous rigid guardrail, three vehicles are traveling at night under dry road conditions. V1 is in lane 2, positioned ahead of the others, moving uphill at a steady 75 km/h with a cruising intent. V2 follows V1 in the same lane 2 at a distance of approximately 25 meters, maintaining a coordinated speed of 75 km/h and intending to keep a safe following distance. V3 is in lane 3, slightly behind V2 by about 10 meters, traveling at 78 km/h and gradually closing the gap with the intention to overtake V2 while maintaining smooth speed coordination with surrounding traffic.

Scenario Development
As all vehicles proceed uphill, the incline reduces engine efficiency, causing V1’s speed to gradually drop from 75 km/h to 68 km/h despite maintaining throttle. V2 detects the deceleration and lightly reduces speed to 70 km/h, attempting to preserve a safe following distance. However, due to the uphill gradient, the relative speed difference compresses the gap more quickly than expected. Meanwhile, V3, traveling in lane 3, observes V2’s slight deceleration and adjusts speed from 78 km/h to 72 km/h to maintain speed coordination and avoid overtaking too aggressively in low-visibility night conditions.

At this moment, V1 suddenly performs emergency braking, reducing speed sharply from 68 km/h to 30 km/h due to a perceived obstruction ahead near the guardrail (though not visible to following vehicles). This abrupt deceleration forces V2 into a critical situation: despite initially maintaining a safe following distance, the combination of uphill dynamics and delayed visual recognition at night reduces available reaction time. V2 applies strong braking, dropping from 70 km/h to 35 km/h, but the reduced stopping efficiency on the incline and compressed spacing make full avoidance difficult.

Simultaneously, V3 observes V2’s brake lights and reacts by braking from 72 km/h to 40 km/h. However, because V3 is positioned slightly offset in lane 3 and had been preparing to overtake, its lateral position limits immediate evasive options, especially with the rigid guardrail on the left preventing any further leftward maneuver. V3’s deceleration influences V2’s decision-making: V2 cannot safely steer left to avoid V1 due to V3’s presence and proximity, and cannot steer right due to lane constraints and stability considerations on the uphill segment.

Result
The sequence culminates in V2 colliding with the rear of V1 at approximately 35 km/h, marking the first impact. The collision occurs in lane 2, involving V1 and V2 directly. V3, having reduced speed significantly, avoids immediate collision but remains in a high-risk proximity behind V2.
